# iliad-036 — new renderings (rows for the table in conventions.md)

No departure from the Odyssey or from an earlier Iliad row. Reused unchanged: 6.9–11 (iliad-026, 4.459–461, third line cut at the full stop), 6.48 (odyssey-102), 6.72 (iliad-031, whole unit), 6.103–105 (iliad-031, whole unit), 6.106 (first half of the iliad-031 unit, same English), 6.67 (iliad-008, 2.110, address line kept, continued into a longer sentence), and the table rows for ἀπερείσι’ ἄποινα, ἠΰν τε μέγαν τε, κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων, ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν, ἀρηΐφιλος, μενεπτόλεμος, οἰωνοπόλων ὄχ’ ἄριστος, ἀγαυός, ἀμύμων, θούριδος ἀλκῆς, αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος, ἤρκεσε λυγρὸν ὄλεθρον, φύλοπις αἰνή, μήστωρ φόβοιο, ἐξενάριξε.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Νέστωρ δ’ Ἀργείοισιν ἐκέκλετο μακρὸν ἀΰσας (6.66; = 6.110 with Ἕκτωρ … Τρώεσσιν; whole-line speech introduction) | "And Nestor to the Argives called out, shouting loudly:" | "And Nestor gave orders to the Argives, shouting loudly:" | "cried to", "shouted aloud and urged"; "gave orders" is the table’s rendering of ἐκέκλετο (Odyssey 6.71, 14.413) and μακρόν is "loudly" as in μακρὸν ἄϋσε (5.347) |
| ἀτυζόμενος / ἀτυζομένω (6.38, 6.41; ἀτύζομαι, struck with panic) | "dazed with fear" | "dazed with fear" | "bewildered", "terrified" (kept for ταρβέω), "panic-stricken" |
| ἀκήδεστοι καὶ ἄφαντοι (6.60; ἀκήδεστος from κῆδος "care", echoing κήδεαι in 6.55) | "unmourned and unseen" | "unmourned and unseen" | "uncared-for", "without burial", "vanished"; "unseen" keeps ἄφαντος as "not to be seen" |
| ἀναλκείη (6.74, dative plural; ἀν- + ἀλκή) | "want of might" | "want of might" | "cowardice", "weakness", "lack of courage"; follows θούριδος ἀλκῆς "impetuous might" |
| ἠκέστας (6.94, of heifers; the sense is not known with certainty) | "never-goaded" | "never touched by the goad" (+ note: sense not known, traditionally read as not yet broken to work) | "unbroken", "untamed", "unblemished" |
| ἤνις (6.94) | "year-old" | "yearling" | "young" |
| ζώγρει (6.46; ζωγρέω "take alive") | "Take me alive" | "Take me alive" | "spare me", "make me prisoner" |
| ἔπειθε (imperfect of πείθω, 6.51, in the formula ὣς φάτο, τῷ δ’ ἄρα θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἔπειθε) | "So he spoke, and in him the heart in his breast he was persuading;" | "So he spoke, and he was winning over the heart in Menelaus’ breast;" | "convinced"; follows the table’s ὄρινε line (4.208), with the imperfect shown by "was" |
| αἴσιμα παρειπών (6.62) | "fitting things having talked-over" | "talking him round with what was fitting" | "persuading with sound words", "advising rightly"; αἴσιμα kept as "fitting" (cf. ἐναίσιμον "of what is fitting") |
| ἀντίος ἦλθε θέων (6.53–54) | "opposite came running" | "came running to meet him" | "ran up against", "advanced against" |
| εἶπε παραστάς (6.75) | "had spoken, standing beside them" | "stood beside … and spoken to them" | "came up and said"; παραστάς "standing beside" as in 2.188 |
| λὰξ ἐν στήθεσι βάς (6.65) | "with his heel on his chest, having stepped" | "setting his heel on his chest" | "kicking", "trampling", "planting his foot" |
| σκότιον (6.24, adverbial; "in the dark", of a birth out of wedlock) | "in secret" | "in secret" (+ note: σκότιος "in the dark") | "illegitimately" (names the status, not the Greek), "secretly" |
| φόως ἑτάροισιν ἔθηκεν (6.6) | "light to his companions made" | "brought his companions light" (+ note: light = relief) | "gave respite", "saved" (flattens the image) |
| Νεστορίδης (6.33) | "the son of Nestor" | "son of Nestor" | "Nestor’s son" |
| ἀγκύλον ἅρμα (6.39) | "the curved chariot" | "the curved chariot" | "bent", "crooked" (the table’s καμπύλον ἅρμα is "bent") |
| δηΐοισι … χάρμα (6.82) | "a joy to the enemy" | "a joy to our enemies" | "delight of the foe" |
| ἐν χερσὶ γυναικῶν (6.81) | "in the hands of women" | "into the arms of their women" | "at the mercy of women" |
| πᾶσαν ἐπ’ ἰθύν (6.79) | "on every straight course" | "at every turn" | "in every direction", "in all things" |
| ἐποτρύνητον (dual, 6.83) | "have urged on" (with "you two") | "have urged on" (with "you two") | "rallied", "stirred up" |
| ὁμοκλήσας ἔπος ηὔδα (6.54) | "having shouted at him spoke a word" | "shouting at him, said" | "rebuked him loudly"; ὁμοκλήσας as in the table’s δεινὰ δ’ ὁμοκλήσας "dreadfully having shouted at him" |
